media:group.media:title: Boiling Point: 52 Days Survival (Full Story)
media:group.media:description:
One morning the sun flares, and by 3PM your father's thermometer reads 173°F. You, your daughter and your old father hide in your grandfather's storm cellar.
All three parts of Boiling Point in one film, from the first flare to the first night without frost.
▶ Our other full movie, Absolute Zero: https://youtu.be/pKJoeiTGDeE
This is a fictional story. The science in it is real: • 173°F (78°C) is hotter than any air temperature ever measured on Earth. • A person sitting still gives off about as much heat as a 100-watt light bulb. Sixteen people in a cellar are a heater that never switches off. • Dry air can't hold the day's heat. In a desert, it can get 40°F (22°C) colder in a single night.

media:group.media:title: Boiling Point: 40 Days Survival (Final Part)
media:group.media:description:
▶ The full movie, all 3 parts in one: https://youtu.be/bg1k9B8w7Dg
At eight in the morning, a wall of water tears the road away, and your farm is cut off. Until the grass grows back, every noon is hot enough to kill you and every night cold enough to freeze, and all you have left is an old camper trailer, two propane tanks and a well.
The last part of Boiling Point. It works as a standalone episode, but it's best watched after Parts 1 and 2.
A fictional story. The science in it is real: • Dry air can't hold the day's heat. In a desert, it can get 40°F (22°C) colder in a single night. • Parked in the sun, a closed car warms up by about 40°F (22°C) within an hour. • More than 2,000 years ago, people in the Persian desert made ice on cold nights and kept it through the summer in domed ice houses called yakhchals.

entry.title: Absolute Zero: 30 Days Survival in a Frozen City (Full Story)

media:group.media:title: Absolute Zero: 30 Days Survival in a Frozen City (Full Story)
media:group.media:description:
Night 1: the city freezes at −100°C, the power goes out, and at nine o'clock someone upstairs knocks on the heating pipe. For the next month, you and your husky Bear go from a frozen apartment to a sauna on the hill to an old hangar at the air base, and every night at nine, the knocking follows you.
▶ Our other full movie, Boiling Point: https://youtu.be/bg1k9B8w7Dg
All four parts of Absolute Zero in one film: 30 days in about an hour, from the first knock to the last.
A fictional story. The science in it is real: • Water grows about 9% bigger when it freezes. That's what bursts pipes and splits trees. • In deep cold, the water in a fire's smoke freezes into a white plume you can see for miles. • Below about −58°F (−50°C), you can hear your breath freeze. In Yakutia they call it "the whisper of the stars".

media:group.media:title: What if the Sun starts to kill? #survivalstory #zombieapocalypse #extremeweather #survivalhorror
Boiling Point: 7 Days Survival (Part 2)
media:group.media:description:
▶ The full movie, all 3 parts in one: https://youtu.be/bg1k9B8w7Dg
Last summer, the sun burned your farm to the ground. Now the radio says it's coming back, even hotter, and you have one day to get ready. At sunrise, twelve strangers knock on your door, and your cellar can keep only six people alive.
This is a stickman survival short movie and the sequel to Boiling Point. It works as a standalone episode, but it's best watched after the first movie.
This is a fictional story. The science in it is real: • Scientists can see storms on the far side of the sun by listening to the sound waves that travel through it. Seen from Earth, the sun turns once about every 27 days. • A day's heat gets only about a foot into the ground, so every extra foot of earth over your head buys time. • Firefighters stop wildfires with fire: a burnout burns the grass in front of the flames, so they have nothing left to eat. • A person sitting still gives off about as much heat as a 100-watt light bulb. Sixteen people are a space heater that never switches off. • In dry air, sweat dries on your skin and cools you. In air full of water it can't, and 100°F (38°C) can kill.
CHAPTERS 0:00 The sun is coming back 1:53 One day to get ready 4:13 Twelve strangers at the door 7:24 The knock at noon 10:50 The fifth night
Twelve strangers at sunrise, and room for six. How many would you let in? Tell me in the comments.

entry.title: Absolute Zero: 11 Days Survival in a Frozen City (Final Part)

media:group.media:title: Absolute Zero: 11 Days Survival in a Frozen City (Final Part)
media:group.media:description:
Fourteen people died in that gym. Everyone at the camp says you killed them. Now the last plane out of the cold is leaving, and you're locked in a cell.
SEE FULL MOVIE HERE - https://youtu.be/pKJoeiTGDeE
Part 4 is the final part of Season 1 of Absolute Zero. The army flies 2,000 people out of the air base. Yet the last plane leaves fourteen strangers on the runway, and you behind bars. At −100°C, you break out and lead them to an old hangar: a brick workshop, an iron stove, and something big under a tarp. The old man says she can still fly. All you need is a few hours. And every night at nine, everyone looks at the door. And then at you.
This is a fictional story. The science in it is real: • Deep cold makes ordinary steel brittle. In January 1943, the brand-new tanker SS Schenectady cracked in two at its dock in Portland, Oregon. • Never touch metal with bare skin in deep cold: the skin freezes to it. • Below about −50°C you can hear your breath freeze. In Yakutia they call it "the whisper of the stars". • Hot air rises. In a huge room, a bigger fire only heats the roof. • A resting person gives off about 100 watts of heat, like a 100-watt bulb. • Frostbite: don't rub it, and don't warm it at a stove or fire. Numb skin can't feel the heat, so it burns. Warm it slowly, in your armpits. • Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so a candle on the floor shows you when the air goes bad. • Airport jet fuel (Jet A-1) turns to slush at about −47°C. The air force's old JP-4, used until the mid-1990s, stays liquid down to about −60°C. • Cold drains a battery, and a frozen lead-acid battery can crack.
